issue_snapshot.title: Bootable Next.js shell with database, health and pipeline verbs
issue_snapshot.body:
Anyone can boot the app locally and CI can verify it, proving the Vercel and Postgres foundation before any product code lands.

Person sees: a bootable app shell (home placeholder) plus /api/health proving database reachability, styled from the token set. Contract: this slice DEFINES getDb() (PGlite when DATABASE_URL unset, neon-serverless WebSocket Pool when set, opened and closed per request including on error with nothing at module scope), the Drizzle schema and automatic SQL migration mechanism, GET /api/health {status, db, latencyMs}, env-var secrets with safe local defaults and loud production failure, and makes sdlc:verify, sdlc:serve, sdlc:seed and sdlc:ready real. Constraints: TR-1 serverless-only, TR-2 same migrations on both backends, invariant that only getDb() branches on backend.

**Risk.** Infra/migration risk: Drizzle schema as single source of truth, same SQL migrations on PGlite and Neon, per-request neon-serverless Pool open and close with nothing at module scope; no code outside getDb() may branch on backend.

**Out of scope**
- Accounts and sessions
- Groups, expenses, balances and activity product screens
- Seed data and Vercel deploy beyond the health and boot path

Covers: TR-1, TR-2, TR-5, TR-12
Part of #1.

## Acceptance (from the split)
- **IAC-1** Boot with DATABASE_URL unset via sdlc:serve and open the home page with no crash; the boot log notes safe local defaults
- **IAC-2** GET /api/health returns status ok with db ok plus latencyMs, and sdlc:ready passes against the booted app
- **IAC-3** sdlc:verify passes (npm ci, typecheck, Vitest suite, Next.js build) and production refuses to boot with a message naming any missing required secret

## Decisions (recorded by the pipeline)

- **replan-project** by @Shivam-Fl (2026-10-04T16:12:18.702Z):
  Approve with three changes; keep everything else as it is. (1) Neon driver: use Drizzle's neon-serverless driver (a Pool from @neondatabase/serverless over WebSocket) when DATABASE_URL is set, not the http driver. The http driver cannot hold an interactive transaction, and creating, editing or deleting an expense must write the expense, its payers, its shares and its activity entry atomically (TR-8: never half-written). Update ADR-0002, the getDb() interface, and TR-2's proof: the Neon smoke test runs one transaction that rolls back on error and leaves nothing behind. (2) Store the split rule with the expense, not only its result: the split type on Expense, and on each split line the member's input as entered (exact amount, percentage or share count, and whether they were included) beside the computed share. The edit form reopens showing exactly what was entered. Balances still read only the stored payer parts and computed shares. Add it to the data model, the expense editor in docs/ui.md, and an ADR. (3) The spec says every change is recorded 'with who made it and what changed': an expense-edited activity entry stores a structured before/after of the fields that changed (description, amount, date, payers, participants, split type and inputs, category, note), written in the same transaction as the edit. Say so in TR-10 and the ActivityEvent model.
- **replan-project** by @Shivam-Fl (2026-10-04T16:25:43.988Z):
  All three changes are in; thank you. One addition, then I approve: the Pool's lifecycle on Vercel. A WebSocket Pool must not outlive the request that uses it on serverless (Neon's guidance for @neondatabase/serverless): getDb() on the Neon side opens the Pool for the request and closes it when the request's work is done, including after an error, and nothing holds a Pool or client at module scope. Say this in the getDb() interface in docs/trd.md and in ADR-0002. And since CI and QA run on PGlite only, add an invariant that no code may branch on which backend it is running against except getDb() itself, so a Neon-only code path cannot hide from the tests. Keep everything else as it is.

acceptance.check: With DATABASE_URL unset, `npm run sdlc:serve` boots, the boot log notes safe local defaults (PGlite, dev-only secret), and the home page at http://localhost:3000 renders the Tabs placeholder with no crash
acceptance.how_to_verify: QA runs sdlc:serve capturing output to a file, greps the safe-defaults line, opens / in a browser

acceptance.check: GET /api/health returns 200 `{status:'ok', db:'ok', latencyMs:<non-negative number>}` by reading the schema_migrations ledger on the serving instance (not SELECT 1), proving boot migrations applied to the instance that serves traffic
acceptance.how_to_verify: QA curls /api/health and asserts the JSON shape; stopping the server and deleting any local state then rebooting still returns ok

acceptance.check: `npm run sdlc:ready` exits 0 against the booted app
acceptance.how_to_verify: QA boots via sdlc:serve then runs sdlc:ready

acceptance.check: `npm run sdlc:verify` passes end to end on a fresh clone: npm ci (lockfile committed), tsc --noEmit, full Vitest suite, Next.js production build
acceptance.how_to_verify: CI runs sdlc:verify on a clean runner

acceptance.check: With VERCEL_ENV=production and SESSION_SECRET unset, boot refuses with an error naming SESSION_SECRET; with VERCEL_ENV=production and DATABASE_URL blank or unset, boot refuses naming DATABASE_URL; local `next build`/`next start` via sdlc:serve with no secrets still boots on safe defaults (guard is never keyed on NODE_ENV alone)
acceptance.how_to_verify: QA runs the production-shaped boot with each secret missing and reads the failure message, then boots normally via sdlc:serve

acceptance.check: The same SQL migration set applies automatically at boot on a fresh database, is re-runnable without error (version insert is conflict-safe, filenames immutable), and a failing transaction leaves no rows behind and no ledger entry
acceptance.how_to_verify: Vitest migrate/transaction cases on PGlite in CI; manual scripts/neon-smoke.ts against a real Neon URL

acceptance.check: The app ships as one Next.js App Router production build served by `next start` on port 3000 with no background process and no durable local disk use; the migration SQL ships inside the server bundle (trace include or generated index), proven from the build artefact rather than the source tree
acceptance.how_to_verify: QA drives the production build served by sdlc:serve; review rejects disk/process code and checks the trace/index

acceptance.check: Missing secrets fall back to logged safe local defaults unless VERCEL_ENV=production, where they throw naming the variable; blank/whitespace DATABASE_URL counts as unset for backend selection
acceptance.how_to_verify: Vitest lib/env.test.ts and lib/db/client.test.ts cases run in CI

acceptance.check: `npm run sdlc:seed` exits 0 after running migrations and ships no fixture rows; the README states fixture rows belong to the seed ticket, so TR-12's seed proof stays open and this criterion cannot be misread as meeting it
acceptance.how_to_verify: Seed run plus reviewer reads README against a fresh clone

acceptance.check: No non-test source file outside lib/db/client.ts references DATABASE_URL, PGlite, neon-serverless or ws; drizzle.config.ts and scripts/neon-smoke.ts obtain the connection string only through the helper exported by client.ts; enforced by a failing-if-violated test scoped to app/**, lib/** and scripts/** (excluding *.test.ts and neon-smoke.ts) so docs, plan and build artefacts cannot trip it
acceptance.how_to_verify: Vitest lib/db/backend-invariant.test.ts scans the scoped set in CI

alternatives_considered.approach: Run migrations with drizzle-kit CLI migrate commands configured per driver
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Needs a DATABASE_URL-aware CLI config per backend, which is itself a second branch on backend outside getDb(); a single custom SQL-file applier over the shared db.execute interface needs no branch at all.

alternatives_considered.approach: Use Drizzle's neon-http driver for the Neon side (simpler, no WebSocket, no ws dependency)
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Already rejected in ADR-0002 and the binding replan-project decision: one-shot HTTP requests hold no session, so expense create/edit/delete could not commit expense, payers, split lines and activity atomically in one interactive transaction (TR-8).

alternatives_considered.approach: Apply migrations at build time (Vercel build command) instead of at runtime boot
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The build environment does not reliably carry the runtime pooled DATABASE_URL (previews especially); registering migrations on server boot via instrumentation.ts covers every instance with an idempotent runner.

alternatives_considered.approach: Leave sdlc:seed a stub for the seed ticket
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The admitted issue contract says this slice 'makes sdlc:verify, sdlc:serve, sdlc:seed and sdlc:ready real'; a stub would contradict the ticket, so the verb goes real but honestly minimal with fixtures deferred.

validated_work_order.approach: Greenfield skeleton: replace the four stub verbs with real scripts, add a minimal Next.js App Router shell (placeholder home styled from the ui.md tokens, GET /api/health using only Web-standard Request/Response so it is unit-testable and reading the migration ledger so it proves the serving instance migrated), and a lib/db layer that is the only place allowed to know which backend is active. getDb() returns a { db, close, backend } handle: when DATABASE_URL is unset or blank, a process-scoped PGlite singleton (with memoized migration state) shared across requests in dev/CI/QA; when set, a neon-serverless WebSocket Pool opened per call and closed per request including on error. Production is keyed on VERCEL_ENV=production, never on NODE_ENV alone (Next sets NODE_ENV=production for every build and start, which would otherwise make the safe-defaults boot and the production guard mutually exclusive), and in production a missing or blank DATABASE_URL throws naming it. Migrations are plain SQL files applied at boot by a backend-agnostic runner (db.execute only, CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ledger bootstrap, each file in its own transaction, version insert ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, filenames immutable) invoked from an instrumentation.ts register() guarded on NEXT_RUNTIME=nodejs and from npm run db:migrate / db:seed; the SQL set ships in the server bundle via tracing include or a generated index. env handling lives in lib/env.ts (zod, SESSION_SECRET only, no DATABASE_URL and no backend references); the db layer reports the backend it selected and instrumentation logs it. The first migration creates only the ledger table; domain tables belong to later tickets. A scoped source-scanning test enforces the only-getDb-branches invariant, and scripts/neon-smoke.ts (manual, needs a real DATABASE_URL, reads it only via the client.ts helper) proves the Neon transaction-rollback behavior CI cannot reach on PGlite.
assumptions: npm registry is reachable from CI so the first install can generate the lockfile that later `npm ci` runs consume
@neondatabase/serverless Pool construction is lazy (no connection until first query), so constructing-and-closing a Pool with an untrusted DATABASE_URL in tests does not touch the network
Setting neonConfig.webSocketConstructor = ws inside the getDb module is sufficient for the Node serverless runtime; the global WebSocket alone is not relied on
PGlite runs fully in-process with no native bindings or background process, satisfying the CI clean-runner (node/npm only) constraint
QA boots via `npm run sdlc:serve` against localhost:3000 per .sdlc/config.yml env.boot (the full build in serve is accepted per ADR-0006)
Next 16 needs no instrumentation flag (instrumentation is stable since 15) and honors the NEXT_RUNTIME guard; implementer verifies both keys against the installed Next version
validated_work_order.confidence_rationale: The stack is standard and documented (Next + Drizzle + PGlite + neon-serverless) and the critique's evidence checked out against the repo (no lockfile, no instrumentation flag, QA boots without secrets), so the two load-bearing fixes (VERCEL_ENV guard, PGlite singleton plus ledger-reading health) rest on verified facts; docked because exact Next 16 config keys, neon-serverless packaging, and drizzle-kit journal behavior must be re-verified against the installed packages at implement time, and the Neon rollback proof stays manual-only.
validated_work_order.debate_summary: The critique was right on diagnosis in six places and the plan is rewritten around them: (1) BLOCKING — the NODE_ENV production guard collides with Next setting NODE_ENV=production for every build/start, making AC-1 and AC-5 mutually exclusive; guard rekeyed to VERCEL_ENV=production and AC-5 rewritten. (2) PGlite per-request open/close wipes data every request and makes boot migrations decorative; adopted as a process-scoped PGlite singleton with conflict-safe ledger inserts, while the Neon Pool stays strictly per-request — read narrowly, the binding 'nothing at module scope' decision targets the Neon Pool on serverless (PGlite never runs in production per ADR-0002), so this honors its intent. (3) The invariant scan's allowlist and scope were self-contradictory (test file, smoke script, drizzle config and docs all contain the strings); rescoped to app/lib/scripts excluding tests, with connection string flowing only through a client.ts helper. (4) env.ts logging the backend violated the invariant it was allowlisted in; the db layer now reports the backend and instrumentation logs it, env.ts carries no backend references. (5) instrumentationHook is not a Next 16 top-level option and register() lacked the documented NEXT_RUNTIME guard; flag dropped, guard added. (6) Runtime-read SQL is invisible to output tracing (green locally, ENOENT on Vercel) and the repo has no lockfile for the `npm ci` verb; both fixed in files. Rejected: leaving sdlc:seed a stub (the admitted issue explicitly makes all four verbs real; kept honestly minimal instead with TR-12 seed proof deferred), and the claim that lib/db/migrations is a framework-reserved path (grep over .sdlc/bin/detect.js finds no 'migrations' rule and config.yml forbidden_paths lists none — unfounded). The ledger triple-ownership and drizzle numbering fears are reduced to implement-time checks plus ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and an immutability note rather than a directory reshuffle. Edge cases folded in: blank DATABASE_URL, production-requires-DATABASE_URL, ledger-reading health, boot-log observability, race-safe re-application; timeouts, malformed-URL surfacing and cold-start migration latency stay residual risks.

files.change: postcss config wiring @tailwindcss/postcss

files.change: GET handler using only global Request/Response (no next/server import, stays unit-testable): times a ledger read (SELECT against schema_migrations, proving the serving instance applied boot migrations), returns 200 {status:'ok',db:'ok',latencyMs} on success and 503 {status:'degraded',db:'down',latencyMs} on any error
files.why: TR-12 health proof with latencyMs; ledger read (not SELECT 1) proves migration wiring, and the 503 body keeps curl -fsS (sdlc:ready) red exactly when the DB is down

files.change: zod-parsed env for app secrets (SESSION_SECRET with dev-only fallback); production means VERCEL_ENV=production, never NODE_ENV alone; logs safe defaults outside production and throws 'Missing required secret: <NAME>' in production. Must not reference DATABASE_URL, PGlite, neon-serverless or ws in any form.
files.why: TR-5 single choke point for app secrets without becoming a second backend brancher; Next sets NODE_ENV=production on every local build/start so it cannot signal production

files.change: getDb(): Promise<{db, close, backend}> — the ONLY place that branches on backend. Trims DATABASE_URL (empty/whitespace counts as unset); in production (VERCEL_ENV=production) a missing/blank DATABASE_URL throws naming it. Unset: process-scoped PGlite singleton (plus memoized migration state) shared across requests, close is a no-op. Set: neon-serverless Pool opened per call via withDb(fn) try/finally close, including on error; no Pool or client held at module scope. Exports the shared Db union type plus a helper exposing the selected backend/connection string for tests, smoke script and drizzle config.
files.why: The contract this slice DEFINES: per-request Neon Pool lifecycle including on error, durable PGlite across requests in dev/CI/QA, production refuses PGlite-by-misconfiguration

files.change: runMigrations(db): CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ledger bootstrap, read lib/db/migrations/*.sql in sorted order, apply each pending file with db.execute inside db.transaction and record its version with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; same code path for both backends; comment states an applied filename is immutable and drizzle-kit generate must be re-run clean after any schema edit
files.why: Automatic same-SQL-migrations mechanism (TR-2) with zero backend branching and race-safe re-application across concurrent cold starts

files.change: Drizzle pgTable definition of schema_migrations(version text PK, applied_at timestamptz default now) exported for drizzle-kit generate consistency with a comment that it is the operational ledger, not a domain table; domain tables land in later tickets
files.why: Drizzle schema as single source of truth starts here; ledger is the only table this slice owns

files.change: SQL creating schema_migrations if not exists (matches schema.ts); the runner records itself here
files.why: First migration proving the generate-and-apply loop end to end

files.change: drizzle-kit config: schema ./lib/db/schema.ts, out ./lib/db/migrations, dialect postgresql (generate-only; applying is the custom runner); obtains any connection string only via the helper exported from lib/db/client.ts
files.why: Keeps future schema edits generating SQL into the same directory the runner applies, without becoming a second backend brancher

files.change: vitest config: node environment, include lib/**/*.test.ts and app/**/*.test.ts, no browser/server
files.why: test:ci runner for the colocated suite (repo rule: no test needs network or a real server)

files.change: tsx entry calling runMigrations() inside withDb then exiting; used by db:migrate and at deploy time
files.why: Manual/CI migration entry independent of booting the app

files.change: tsx entry running migrations then logging that the skeleton slice ships no fixture rows (full seed fixtures belong to the seed ticket) and exiting 0
files.why: Makes sdlc:seed a real verb now without smuggling the out-of-scope seed data into this ticket

files.change: Manual-only tsx script (requires real DATABASE_URL, never run in CI, obtains it only via the client.ts helper): opens a transaction inserting a ledger probe row, throws, then asserts the probe row is absent; logs clean rollback or fails
files.why: TR-2 proof for the Neon side that CI cannot reach on PGlite-only runners, per the binding decision

Accounts/sessions, groups, expenses, balances, activity product screens and tables

Words in docs/spec, docs/prd.md, docs/trd.md, docs/ui.md and .sdlc/memory: already updated for the Neon Pool lifecycle, split-rule storage and edited-entry before/after via the project brief; tickets must not touch those paths
qa_auth mode decision (open question in project.md) — no login exists in this slice

validated_work_order.understanding: Issue #3 is the bootable-foundation slice: a Next.js shell (home placeholder + GET /api/health {status,db,latencyMs}), the getDb() contract (PGlite when DATABASE_URL unset, neon-serverless WebSocket Pool when set, Neon Pool opened/closed per request including on error), the Drizzle schema plus automatic same-SQL-migrations mechanism, env secrets with safe local defaults and loud production failure, and real sdlc:verify/serve/seed/ready verbs — under TR-1/TR-2/TR-5/TR-12, the backend invariant (only getDb() branches), and the two binding replan-project decisions (neon-serverless Pool with per-request lifecycle; split-rule storage and edited-entry before/after already recorded in the approved docs). The repo is greenfield (package.json holds only the four stub verbs), so there are no existing callers to preserve and no prior plan rejection to answer.
unknowns: Whether @neondatabase/serverless on Node 22 strictly requires the ws package or works on the global WebSocket — the plan includes ws regardless, so either outcome works

Exact Next 16 config key names for the server-bundle include and register() timing under `next start` — verified against the installed packages at implement time; the db:migrate script is the fallback entry
